items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.desc: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recordedMultiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...

items.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
items.desc: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

items.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
items.desc: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.

items.title: New day of protests across France
items.desc: France faces a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators taking to the streets to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.

items.title: Cargo ship runs aground off French coast
items.desc: A Maltese-flagged cargo ship remains stranded off the coast of south-western France after running aground. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent the vessel from capsizing and potentially causing pollution. The ship was not carrying any cargo, and all 19 crew members were safely evacuated by helicopter. Dan Quinlan reports.

items.title: Russia tests NATO’s eastern defences
items.desc: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk said was likely an "intentional provocation" timed to coincide with European military exercises in the country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. Senior Lecturer in Conflict and Security at King's College in London, Domitilla Sagramoso, shares further insights.

items.title: Thousands protest overs prices, education, military spending in France and Europe
items.desc: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us the latest from Paris.

items.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
items.desc: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after a drone strike in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish ⁠territorial waters, Finnish authorities said. Helsinki alerted NATO and imposed temporary restrictions in the area amid heightened tensions in the Baltic Sea.

items.title: Ethiopia: Tackling period poverty and stigma
items.desc: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is tackling period poverty and the stigma surrounding menstruation. By producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and raising awareness in schools, she hopes to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class. Report by Awa Diouf & Guillaume Gougeon.

items.title: Ethiopia - Eritrea: Troops mobilise along the border
items.desc: More than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military Friday, state-affiliated media reported, amid escalating border tensions with neighboring Eritrea. France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti tells us the latest.

items.title: Music strikes a chord at French protest
items.desc: Throughout history, protest songs have brought people together across genres, rallying against war, racism, inequality and the establishment. Music is also playing a key role in the youth-led demonstrations here in France. Our reporters went to meet some of the musicians using their voices to express the protesters’ demands.

items.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
items.desc: A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.

items.title: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US
items.desc: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an alleged Russian intelligence plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, vowing full solidarity with Copenhagen.

items.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
items.desc: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

items.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
items.desc: Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.

items.title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.desc: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.

items.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
items.desc: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

items.title: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway
items.desc: A chance for revenge. Beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals last July, France will meet La Roja again in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.

items.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
items.desc: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.

items.title: 【世界进行时】2026年11月20日
items.desc: 本期要点：国际法院裁定缅甸对罗兴亚人实施种族灭绝；古特雷斯呼吁就“杀人机器人”制定具有法律约束力的文书；苏丹：无人机袭击激增对平民造成的致命影响；儿基会：全球每四分钟就有一名儿童死于暴力；联合国报告：干扰内分泌化学物质可能在出生前影响人体健康；经巴拿马北上人流减少九成，拉美移民转向新路线。

items.title: 【前方视野】1.5摄氏度临界点逼近：中国如何回答气候变化时代的转型之问
items.desc: 从工业革命以来，人类从未像今天这样清晰地感受到自身活动与地球系统之间的关联。持续刷新的高温纪录、愈发频繁的极端天气，都在提醒国际社会，应对气候变化的窗口正在收窄。在土耳其举行的第31届联合国气候变化框架公约缔约方大会（COP31）上，各国围绕减排目标、能源转型、气候融资和绿色贸易展开激烈讨论。面对全球升温可能在未来十年内跨越1.5摄氏度关键门槛的警示，中国国家气候变化专家委员会副主任王毅在接受《联合国新闻》专访时表示，气候行动已进入更加注重落实的新阶段，而中国正在通过全面绿色转型、新型能源体系建设、绿色低碳技术创新及法律制度建设，为长期绿色低碳发展探索了一条具有自身特色的路径。

items.title: 约旦河西岸：定居者袭击事件创纪录  联合国敦促以色列保护农民
items.desc: 联合国机构和人道主义非政府组织周五表示，在今年被占领的约旦河西岸橄榄收获季期间，以色列定居者发动了400多次袭击，造成人员伤亡或财产损失——这一数字超过了以往任何一个收获季。

items.title: 粮食署计划2027年援助9100万人
items.desc: 世界粮食计划署周五表示，计划在2027年为9100万人提供援助，需要121亿美元资金。该机构警告，资金持续短缺将使更多人陷入饥饿，新一轮全球粮食危机可能正在逼近。

items.title: 教科文组织：学前教育每投入1美元，到2035年可获近4美元回报
items.desc: 联合国教科文组织周五发布报告指出，过去十年，全球学前教育普及几乎停滞不前。进入小学的儿童中，仅约六成接受过至少一年的学前教育。资金不足和持续存在的不平等，使数百万幼儿难以获得优质保育和教育。

items.title: 支离破碎的游乐场和冰冷的教室：乌克兰儿童遭遇最惨重的一年
items.desc: 在基辅一所两度遭轰炸的幼儿园废墟中，停电已持续一整天。联合国儿童基金会周五指出，随着儿童伤亡人数攀升至创纪录水平，在乌克兰度过又一个严酷冬天的儿童正面临巨大危险。

items.title: 阿富汗的限制措施阻碍孕妇寻求医疗救助
items.desc: 阿富汗援助与发展机构周五警告称，针对妇女和女童权利与自由的侵犯行为日益加剧，这导致越来越多的妇女和女童无法获得至关重要的医疗护理。

items.title: 【子午播报】2026年11月20日

items.title: 【专题报道 | 前方视野】从“丢弃”迈向“循环“时代：零废弃物议程试图打开气候行动的新突破口
items.desc: 在联合国气候变化大会的谈判大厅里，焦点往往集中在能源转型、气候融资和减排目标上。然而，正在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第31届气候变化大会凸显了气候行动中一个长期被低估的领域：通过减少废弃物和推动循环经济来实现减排，这些举措正在成为减缓全球变暖见效快、成本低且极具现实可行性的突破口之一。

items.title: 联合国警告：人工智能正被用于诱骗和剥削儿童
items.desc: 联合国周四警告，人工智能正被侵害者和犯罪团伙用于诱骗、勒索和剥削儿童，而相应保护措施未能跟上技术发展的步伐。

items.title: 联合国：全球电子政务持续推进  但数字鸿沟依然存在
items.desc: 联合国经济和社会事务部周四发布的《2026年联合国电子政务调查报告》指出，全球数字政府发展持续推进，但网络连接、技能和机构能力方面的差距仍在限制数字化带来的效益。随着人工智能重塑公共行政，各国在电子政务发展方面的不平衡依然明显。

items.title: COP31：最新协议草案删去摆脱化石燃料相关表述
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会原定闭幕前夕，最新协议草案删去了逐步摆脱化石燃料的明确表述，引发民间团体不满。各方周四继续就资金、适应和公正转型等关键议题磋商，力争在周五前弥合分歧。

items.title: 国际法院认定缅甸对罗兴亚人实施种族灭绝
items.desc: 国际法院周四就冈比亚诉缅甸案作出判决，认定缅甸在2017年若开邦北部的军事清剿行动中，对罗兴亚人实施了种族灭绝。这是该院首次认定一个国家须为实施种族灭绝承担责任。

items.title: 粮农组织：全球粮食供应总体充裕 但市场风险和粮食安全挑战加剧
items.desc: 联合国粮食及农业组织周四发布最新一期《粮食展望》报告指出，全球农产品供应总体充裕，特别是小麦和粗粮，但大米、食糖和植物油的供需平衡趋于紧张。天气变化、物流中断和政策不确定性正增加全球粮食市场风险。同日，粮农组织总干事屈冬玉呼吁加强国际合作，将粮食安全纳入预防和解决冲突的外交努力。

items.title: 货币基金组织总裁：人工智能将成为影响全球竞争力和经济增长的重要因素
items.desc: 国际货币基金组织总裁格奥尔基耶娃周四在中国深圳举行的2026年亚太经合组织经济领导人会议上表示，人工智能正在对全球经济增长产生实质性影响，将成为影响中期竞争力、生产率和经济增长的重要因素。她同时指出，全球通胀上升、公共债务增加以及结构性改革滞后等问题仍对经济前景构成挑战，各国需要加快采取政策行动。

items.title: 联合国人口基金警告：世界正面临辜负下一代的风险
items.desc: 联合国人口基金周三发布的《2026年世界人口状况报告》指出，尽管年轻一代的教育水平、信息获取能力以及对自身权利的认知达到前所未有的高度，但经济不稳定、不平等、排斥、冲突和气候变化等因素，正阻碍数以百万计的年轻人实现人生抱负，使他们难以获得体面的工作、经济独立、住房以及建立家庭的机会。

items.title: 第31届气候变化大会僵局持续，各国启动新一轮“气候承诺核查”
items.desc: 随着在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第31届联合国气候变化大会闭幕时限日益临近，各国于周三启动了一项新的全球性核查，以检验气候承诺是否得到履行。与此同时，各国部长在峰会的一些最棘手问题上仍陷于僵局：谁来买单、全球摆脱化石燃料的速度有多快，以及如果较贫穷国家无力承担，更绿色的未来能否被称为“公正”。

items.title: 经巴拿马北上人流减少九成，拉美移民转向新路线
items.desc: 国际移民组织周三发布报告指出，2026年上半年，经巴拿马达连隘口北上的移民人数较去年同期下降90%。与此同时，部分移民转而南下、返乡或在其他国家定居，拉丁美洲和加勒比地区的迁徙路线与目的地正在发生变化。

items.title: 儿基会：全球每四分钟就有一名儿童死于暴力
items.desc: 第二届消除针对儿童的暴力问题全球部长级会议周三在菲律宾马尼拉召开。联合国儿童基金会呼吁各国，将两年前在波哥大作出的承诺转化为持续投入，推广已被证明有效的措施，保护儿童免遭暴力侵害。

items.title: 也门战事升级导致至少128名儿童伤亡
items.desc: 联合国儿童基金会周三表示，自9月3日也门战事升级以来，至少已有64名儿童死亡、64名儿童受伤。随着塔伊兹、拉赫季等人口密集地区周边战斗持续，伤亡人数可能进一步上升。

items.title: 原子能机构：伊朗核查工作陷入停滞 乌克兰核设施安全风险持续加剧
items.desc: 国际原子能机构总干事格罗西周三在维也纳向理事会介绍机构工作情况时表示，伊朗核查监督工作因无法获取相关信息和进入核设施而陷入停滞，乌克兰军事冲突持续威胁核设施安全，朝鲜核计划也在进一步推进。与此同时，全球核电发展势头增强，原子能机构将继续推动核能和平利用和核技术国际合作。

items.title: 美国等三国麻疹持续传播，泛美卫生组织呼吁加强疫苗接种

items.title: COP31：海洋保护进入谈判议程，落实承诺仍需资金支持

items.title: 苏丹：联合国报告详述无人机袭击激增对平民造成的致命影响

items.title: 冬雨加剧加沙人道危机，援助受限与资金短缺阻碍救援
